___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___

___E:Presidential elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election)___ were held in the United States on November 6, 2012. Incumbent ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and his ___E:running mate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_mate)___ , incumbent Vice President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ , were elected to a second term.  They defeated the ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ ticket of former Governor of Massachusetts ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ and U.S.
Representative ___E:Paul Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ryan)___ of ___E:Wisconsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin)___ .

As the incumbent ___E:president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , Obama secured the ___E:Democratic nomination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries)___ without serious opposition.
The Republicans experienced a ___E:competitive primary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries)___ .

Romney was consistently competitive in the polls and won the support of many party leaders, but he faced challenges from a number of more ___E:conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States)___ contenders.

Romney secured his party's nomination in May, defeating former senator ___E:Rick Santorum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Santorum)___ , former Speaker of the House and Georgia Congressman ___E:Newt Gingrich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newt_Gingrich)___ , and Texas congressman ___E:Ron Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul)___ , among other candidates.

The campaigns focused heavily on domestic issues, and debate centered largely around sound responses to the ___E:Great Recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession_in_the_United_States)___ along with long-term ___E:federal budget U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_budget)___ issues, the future of ___E:social insurance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_insurance)___ programs, and the ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act)___ . ___E:Foreign policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_United_States)___ was also discussed, including the end of the ___E:Iraq War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War)___ in 2011, military spending, the ___E:Iranian nuclear program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_nuclear_program)___ , and appropriate counteractions to ___E:terrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorism)___ .

Romney claimed Obama's domestic policies were ineffective and financially insolvent while Obama's campaign sought to characterize Romney as a ___E:plutocratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plutocratic)___ businessman who was out of touch with the average American.
The campaign was marked by a sharp rise in fundraising, including from nominally independent ___E:Super PACs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_PACs)___ .

Obama defeated Romney, winning 332 ___E:Electoral College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College)___ votes and 51.1% of the ___E:popular vote U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_by_popular_vote_margin#Table_of_election_results)___ to Romney's 206 electoral votes and 47.2% of the popular vote.  He became the third sitting president in a row (after ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ and ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ ) to win a second term. Obama carried all 18 " ___E:blue wall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_wall_(United_States))___ " states and defeated Romney in crucial ___E:swing states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing_states)___ that Republicans had previously won in ___E:2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ and ___E:2004 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election)___ , namely ___E:Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_Colorado)___ , ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_Florida)___ , ___E:Nevada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_Nevada)___ , ___E:Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_Ohio)___ , and ___E:Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_Virginia)___ .

Despite his loss, Romney managed to flip ___E:Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_Indiana)___ , ___E:North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election_in_North_Carolina)___ , and ___E:Nebraska's 2nd congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska%27s_2nd_congressional_district)___ from the 2008 election.
Ultimately, Obama won eight of the nine main swing states, losing only North Carolina.

As of 2025 [update] , this is the most recent presidential election in which the Democratic candidate won ___E:Iowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa)___ , ___E:Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio)___ , and ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ , along with ___E:Maine's 2nd congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine%27s_2nd_congressional_district)___ .

This also remains the most recent election in which an incumbent president won re-election to a second consecutive term, in which the incumbent presidential party won re-election, and in which neither major party's ticket included a woman.
It is also the most recent presidential election in which the party that won the presidency did not also win control of both chambers of Congress.

In 2011, several state legislatures passed new voting laws, especially pertaining to voter identification, with the stated purpose of combating ___E:voter fraud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_fraud)___ ; however, the laws were attacked by the Democratic Party as attempts to suppress voting among its supporters and to improve the Republican Party's presidential prospects. ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ , ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ , ___E:Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio)___ ,  ___E:Tennessee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee)___ , and ___E:West Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia)___ 's state legislatures approved measures to shorten early voting periods.

Florida and Iowa barred all felons from voting. ___E:Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas)___ , ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ ,  ___E:Tennessee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee)___ , ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ ,  and ___E:Wisconsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin)___  state legislatures passed ___E:laws requiring voters to have government-issued IDs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_ID_laws_(United_States))___ before they could cast their ballots.

This meant typically that people without ___E:driver's licenses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driver%27s_license)___ or ___E:passports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passport)___ had to gain new forms of ID. Former president ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ denounced them, saying, "There has never been in my lifetime, since we got rid of the ___E:poll tax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poll_tax_(United_States))___ and all the ___E:Jim Crow burdens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Crow_laws)___ on voting, the determined effort to limit the franchise that we see today".

He was referring to ___E:Jim Crow laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Crow_laws)___ passed in southern states near the turn of the twentieth century that ___E:disenfranchised U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disfranchisement_after_Reconstruction_era)___ most blacks from voting and excluded them from the political process for more than six decades.

Clinton said the moves would effectively disenfranchise core voter blocs that trend liberal, including college students, ___E:black people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_people)___ , and ___E:Latinos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans)___ .
The Obama campaign fought against the ___E:Ohio law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_Ohio)___ , pushing for a petition and statewide referendum to repeal it in time for the 2012 election.

In addition, the ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania)___ legislature proposed a plan to change its representation in the electoral college from the traditional winner-take-all model to a district-by-district model.
As the governorship and both houses of its legislature were Republican-controlled, the move was viewed by some as an attempt to reduce Democratic chances.
Ultimately, they did not do it, leaving their winner take all format intact as of 2020.
With an incumbent president running for re-election against ___E:token opposition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper_candidate)___ , the race for the Democratic nomination was largely uneventful.

The nomination process consisted of ___E:primaries and caucuses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_primary)___ , held by the 50 states, as well as ___E:Guam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam)___ , ___E:Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico)___ , ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ , ___E:U.S. Virgin Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Virgin_Islands)___ , ___E:American Samoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa)___ , and ___E:Democrats Abroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democrats_Abroad)___ .
Additionally, high-ranking party members known as ___E:superdelegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superdelegate)___ each received one vote in the convention.
A few of the primary challengers surpassed the president's vote total in individual counties in several of the seven contested primaries, though none made a significant impact in the delegate count.

Running unopposed everywhere else, Obama cemented his status as the Democratic ___E:presumptive nominee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presumptive_nominee)___ on April 3, 2012, by securing the minimum number of pledged delegates needed to obtain the nomination.

Candidates with considerable name recognition who entered the race for the Republican presidential nomination in the early stages of the primary campaign included ___E:U.S. representative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ and former Libertarian nominee ___E:Ron Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul)___ , former ___E:Minnesota U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota)___ governor ___E:Tim Pawlenty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Pawlenty)___ , who co-chaired ___E:John McCain's campaign in 2008 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain_2008_presidential_campaign)___ , former ___E:Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts)___ governor ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ , the runner-up for the nomination in the 2008 cycle, and former ___E:Speaker of the House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ ___E:Newt Gingrich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newt_Gingrich)___ .

The first debate took place on May 5, 2011, in ___E:Greenville, South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenville,_South_Carolina)___ , with businessman ___E:Herman Cain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Cain)___ , former New Mexico governor ___E:Gary Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Johnson)___ , ___E:Ron Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul)___ , ___E:Tim Pawlenty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Pawlenty)___ , and former ___E:Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania)___ senator ___E:Rick Santorum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Santorum)___ participating.

Another debate took place a month later, with ___E:Newt Gingrich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newt_Gingrich)___ , ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ , former Utah governor ___E:Jon Huntsman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Huntsman,_Jr.)___ , and Minnesota congresswoman ___E:Michele Bachmann U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Bachmann)___ participating, and Gary Johnson excluded.
A total of ___E:thirteen debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Republican_Party_presidential_debates_and_forums)___ were held before the Iowa caucuses.

The first major event of the campaign was the ___E:Ames Straw Poll U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ames_Straw_Poll)___ , which took place in Iowa on August 13, 2011. Michele Bachmann won the straw poll (this ultimately proved to be the acme of her campaign).

Pawlenty withdrew from the race after a poor showing in the straw poll, as did ___E:Thaddeus McCotter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaddeus_McCotter)___ , the only candidate among those who qualified for the ballot who was refused entrance into the debate.

It became clear at around this point in the nomination process that while Romney was considered to be the likely nominee by the Republican establishment, a large segment of the ___E:conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States)___ primary electorate found him to be too ___E:moderate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moderate)___ for their political views.

As a result, a number of potential "anti-Romney" candidates were put forward,   including future president ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ ,  former Alaska governor and 2008 vice-presidential nominee ___E:Sarah Palin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Palin)___ ,  New Jersey governor ___E:Chris Christie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Christie)___ ,  and Texas governor ___E:Rick Perry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry)___ ,  the last of whom decided to run in August 2011. Perry did poorly in the debates, however, and ___E:Herman Cain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Cain)___ and then ___E:Newt Gingrich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newt_Gingrich)___ came to the fore in October and November.
Due to a number of scandals, Cain withdrew just before the end of the year, after having ballot placement in several states.

Around the same time, Johnson, who had been able to get into only one other debate, withdrew to seek the ___E:Libertarian Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States))___ nomination.

For the first time in modern ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ history, three different candidates won the first three state contests in January (the Iowa caucuses, the New Hampshire primary, and the South Carolina primary).

Although Romney had been expected to win in at least Iowa and New Hampshire, Rick Santorum won the non-binding poll at caucus sites in Iowa by 34 votes, as near as could be determined from the incomplete tally, earning him a declaration as winner by state party leaders, although vote totals were missing from eight precincts.

The election of county delegates at the caucuses would eventually lead to Ron Paul earning 22 of the 28 Iowa delegates to the Republican National Convention.  ___E:Newt Gingrich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newt_Gingrich)___ won South Carolina by a surprisingly large margin,  and Romney won only in New Hampshire.
A number of candidates dropped out at this point in the nomination process.

Bachmann withdrew after finishing sixth in the Iowa caucuses,  Huntsman withdrew after coming in third in New Hampshire, and Perry withdrew when polls showed him drawing low numbers in South Carolina.
Santorum, who had previously run an essentially one-state campaign in Iowa, was able to organize a national campaign after his surprising victory there.

He unexpectedly carried three states in a row on February 7 and overtook Romney in nationwide opinion polls, becoming the only candidate in the race to effectively challenge the notion that Romney was the inevitable nominee.

However, Romney won all of the other contests between South Carolina and the ___E:Super Tuesday primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Tuesday,_2012)___ , and regained his first-place status in nationwide opinion polls by the end of February.

The ___E:Super Tuesday primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Tuesday,_2012)___ took place on March 6. Romney carried six states, Santorum carried three, and Gingrich won only in his home state of Georgia.
Throughout the rest of March, 266 delegates were allocated in 12 events, including the territorial contests and the first local conventions that allocated delegates (Wyoming's county conventions).

Santorum won Kansas and three Southern primaries, but he was unable to make any substantial gain on Romney, who became a formidable frontrunner after securing more than half of the delegates allocated in March.

On April 10, Santorum suspended his campaign due to a variety of reasons, such as a low delegate count, unfavorable polls in his home state of Pennsylvania, and his daughter's health, leaving Mitt Romney as the undisputed front-runner for the presidential nomination and allowing Gingrich to claim that he was "the last conservative standing" in the campaign for the nomination.

After disappointing results in the April 24 primaries (finishing second in one state, third in three, and fourth in one), Gingrich dropped out on May 2 in a move that was seen as an effective end to the contest for the nomination.

After Gingrich's spokesman announced his upcoming withdrawal, the ___E:Republican National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_National_Committee)___ declared Romney the party's ___E:presumptive nominee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presumptive_nominee)___ .
Ron Paul officially remained in the race, but he stopped campaigning on May 14 to focus on state conventions.
On May 29, after winning the Texas primary, Romney had received a sufficient number of delegates to clinch the party's nomination with the inclusion of unpledged delegates.

After winning the June 5 primaries in California and several other states, Romney had received more than enough pledged delegates to clinch the nomination without counting unpledged delegates, making the June 26 Utah Primary, the last contest of the cycle, purely symbolic.
CNN's final delegate estimate, released on July 27, 2012, put Romney at 1,462 pledged delegates and 62 unpledged delegates, for a total estimate of 1,524 delegates.
No other candidate had unpledged delegates.
The delegate estimates for the other candidates were Santorum at 261 delegates, Paul at 154, Gingrich at 142, Bachmann at 1, Huntsman at 1, and all others at 0.
On August 28, 2012, delegates at the ___E:Republican National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_National_Convention)___ officially named Romney the party's presidential nominee.
Romney formally accepted the delegates' nomination on August 30, 2012.

Four other parties nominated candidates that had ballot access or ___E:write-in U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Write-in)___ access to at least 270 electoral votes, the minimum number of votes needed in the 2012 election to win the presidency through a majority of the electoral college.
Candidates in bold were on ballots representing 270 electoral votes.
All other candidates were on the ballots of fewer than 10 states, 100 electors, and less than 20% of voters nationwide.
The United States presidential election of 2012 broke new records in financing, fundraising, and ___E:negative campaigning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negative_campaigning)___ .

Through ___E:grassroots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grassroots)___ campaign contributions, online donations, and ___E:Super PACs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_PACs)___ , Obama and Romney raised a combined total of more than $2 billion.

Super PACs constituted nearly one-fourth of the total financing, with most coming from pro-Romney PACs.  Obama raised $690 million through online channels, beating his record of $500 million in 2008.  Most of the advertising in the 2012 presidential campaign was decidedly negative—80% of Obama's ads and 84% of Romney's ads were negative.

The tax-exempt non-profit ___E:Americans for Prosperity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans_for_Prosperity)___ , a so-called "outside group", that is, a political advocacy group that is not a ___E:political action committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_action_committee)___ or super-PAC, ran a television advertising campaign opposing Obama described by The Washington Post as "early and relentless".

Americans for Prosperity spent $8.4 million in ___E:swing states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing_state)___ on television advertisements denouncing the ___E:American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Recovery_and_Reinvestment_Act_of_2009)___ loan guarantee to ___E:Solyndra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solyndra)___ , a manufacturer of solar panels that went bankrupt,  an advertising campaign described by The Wall Street Journal in November 2011 as "perhaps the biggest attack on Mr. Obama so far".

The ___E:Commission on Presidential Debates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Presidential_Debates)___ held four debates during the last weeks of the campaign: three presidential and one vice-presidential.

The major issues debated were the economy and jobs, the federal budget deficit, taxation and spending, the future of ___E:Social Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States))___ , ___E:Medicare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_(United_States))___ , and ___E:Medicaid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicaid)___ , ___E:healthcare reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patient_Protection_and_Affordable_Care_Act)___ , education, social issues, immigration, and foreign policy.

An independent presidential debate featuring minor party candidates took place on Tuesday, October 23 at the ___E:Hilton Hotel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilton_Hotel)___ in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , Illinois.

The debate was moderated by ___E:Larry King U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King)___  and organized by the ___E:Free & Equal Elections Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_%26_Equal_Elections_Foundation)___ .

The participants were ___E:Gary Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Johnson)___ ( ___E:Libertarian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States))___ ), ___E:Jill Stein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jill_Stein)___ ( ___E:Green U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Party_of_the_United_States)___ ), ___E:Virgil Goode U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil_Goode)___ ( ___E:Constitution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_Party_(United_States))___ ), and ___E:Rocky Anderson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Anderson)___ ( ___E:Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_Party_(United_States))___ ).
A second debate between Stein and Johnson took place on Sunday, November 4, and was moderated by Ralph Nader.

On the day of the election, spread betting firm ___E:Spreadex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spreadex)___ offered an Obama Electoral College Votes spread of 296–300 to Romney's 239–243.  In fact Obama's victory over Romney was greater, winning 332 electoral votes to Romney's 206. Obama received 51 percent of the national popular vote to Romney's 47 percent   and carried eight of the nine states considered to be ___E:electoral battlegrounds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battleground_state)___ .

After the networks called Ohio (the state that was arguably the most critical for Romney, as no Republican had ever won the presidency without carrying it) for Obama at around 11:15 pm ___E:EST U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Standard_Time_(North_America))___ on Election Day, Romney was ready to concede the race, but hesitated when ___E:Karl Rove U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Rove)___ strenuously objected on Fox News to the network's decision to make that call.   However, after Colorado and Nevada were called for the President (giving Obama enough electoral votes to win even if Ohio were to leave his column), in tandem with Obama's apparent lead in Florida and Virginia (both were eventually called for Obama), Romney acknowledged that he had lost and conceded at around 1:00 am ___E:EST U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Standard_Time_(North_America))___ on November 7.

Despite public polling showing Romney behind Obama in the swing states of Nevada, Colorado, Iowa, Wisconsin, Ohio, and New Hampshire, tied with Obama in Virginia, and just barely ahead of Obama in Florida, the Romney campaign said they were genuinely surprised by the loss, having believed that public polling was oversampling Democrats.
The Romney campaign had already set up a transition website, and had scheduled and purchased a fireworks display to celebrate in case he won the election.

On November 30, 2012, it was revealed that shortly before the election, internal polling done by the Romney campaign had shown Romney ahead in Colorado and New Hampshire, tied in Iowa, and within a few points of Obama in Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, and Ohio.  In addition, the Romney campaign had assumed that they would win Florida, North Carolina and Virginia.

The polls had made Romney and his campaign team so confident of their victory that Romney did not write a ___E:concession speech U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concession_(politics))___ until Obama's victory was announced.
Foreign leaders reacted with both positive and mixed messages.
Most world leaders congratulated and praised Obama on his re-election victory.
However, Venezuela and some other states had tempered reactions.
Pakistan commented that Romney's defeat had made ___E:Pakistan-United States relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan-United_States_relations)___ safer.

Stock markets fell noticeably after Obama's re-election, with the ___E:Dow Jones Industrial Average U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average)___ , ___E:NASDAQ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ)___ , and the ___E:S&P 500 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%26P_500)___ each declining over two percent the day after the election.

All 50 states had a petition on the White House website ___E:We The People U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_the_People_(petitioning_system))___ calling for their state to ___E:secede from the union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secession_in_the_United_States)___ .
These petitions were created by individual people, with some gaining thousands of signatures.
